questions.question: Which ancient civilization built the pyramids of Giza?
questions.explanation: The Giza pyramids were built by ancient Egyptians as royal tombs, around 2600–2500 BC.

questions.question: Which empire built the Colosseum in Rome?
questions.explanation: The Colosseum was completed under the Roman Empire in AD 80.

questions.question: Which ancient empire did Cyrus the Great found in the 6th century BC?
questions.explanation: Cyrus united Medes and Persians.

questions.question: Which English king broke with the Roman Catholic Church and founded the Church of England?
questions.explanation: The break came in the 1530s.

questions.question: Which European country ruled Haiti as the colony of Saint-Domingue?
questions.explanation: Saint-Domingue was France's richest colony.

questions.question: How many prisoners were held in the Bastille when it was stormed on 14 July 1789?
questions.explanation: Only seven prisoners were inside: four forgers, two men judged insane and one nobleman.
questions.misconception: Many people think the Bastille was full of political prisoners when it was stormed.

questions.question: Which pandemic killed a huge share of Europe's population in the 1340s and 1350s?
questions.explanation: It is estimated to have killed tens of millions across Eurasia.

questions.question: Who was crowned Emperor of the Romans by Pope Leo III on Christmas Day 800?
questions.explanation: The coronation took place in Rome.

questions.question: In which year did World War II end?
questions.explanation: The war in Europe ended in May 1945 and the war in the Pacific in September 1945.

questions.question: In which year did humans first land on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Apollo 11 landed on 20 July 1969, and Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the surface.

questions.question: Whose assassination in Sarajevo in 1914 set off the First World War?
questions.explanation: The assassination of 28 June 1914 led to Austria-Hungary's ultimatum to Serbia.

questions.question: Which leader is best known for non-violent resistance in India's independence movement?
questions.explanation: Gandhi's methods included boycotts and mass marches.

questions.question: Which system of legal racial segregation did South Africa's National Party formalise from 1948?
questions.explanation: Apartheid classified people by race and separated them by law.

questions.question: How did Napoleon Bonaparte's height compare with that of an average Frenchman of his day?
questions.explanation: He was about 5 pieds 2 pouces in French units, roughly 1.69 m, which was average or slightly above for his time.
questions.misconception: Many people think Napoleon was unusually short.

questions.question: Who was the first President of the United States?
questions.explanation: George Washington served as president from 1789 to 1797.

questions.question: Which West African ruler of the Mali Empire made a famously lavish pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324?
questions.explanation: Mansa Musa's pilgrimage spread so much gold that it was said to have lowered its value in Cairo.

questions.question: Which Chinese admiral led great treasure fleets across the Indian Ocean in the early 1400s?
questions.explanation: Zheng He commanded seven voyages between 1405 and 1433.

questions.question: Which Spanish conquistador captured the Inca emperor Atahualpa in 1532?
questions.explanation: Pizarro seized Atahualpa at Cajamarca.

questions.question: In which city was the House of Wisdom, a great centre of learning under the Abbasid caliphs?
questions.explanation: Baghdad was the Abbasid capital and a hub of translation and science.

questions.question: Which Muslim ruler recaptured Jerusalem from the Crusaders in 1187?
questions.explanation: Saladin took Jerusalem in October 1187.

questions.question: Which civilization built Machu Picchu?
questions.explanation: Machu Picchu was built by the Inca in the 15th century, high in the Peruvian Andes.

questions.question: Which ship carried the Pilgrims from England to America in 1620?
questions.explanation: The Mayflower landed at Cape Cod in November 1620, with about 100 passengers.

questions.question: In which country did the Renaissance begin?
questions.explanation: The Renaissance began in 14th-century Italy, notably in Florence.

questions.question: Who founded the Mongol Empire in 1206?
questions.explanation: Temüjin was proclaimed Genghis Khan in 1206 after uniting the Mongol tribes.

questions.question: In which year was the Battle of Hastings fought?
questions.explanation: William of Normandy defeated King Harold at Hastings in 1066.

questions.question: In which year did the Berlin Wall fall?
questions.explanation: The wall was opened on 9 November 1989, and Germany reunified in 1990.

questions.question: In which year did the French Revolution begin?
questions.explanation: The Revolution began in 1789, famously with the storming of the Bastille on 14 July.

questions.question: The Treaty of Versailles formally ended which war?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Versailles was signed in 1919 and formally ended World War I with Germany.

questions.question: In which country did the Industrial Revolution begin?
questions.explanation: It began in Britain in the 18th century, driven by textiles, coal and steam power.

questions.question: In which year did the Titanic sink?
questions.explanation: The Titanic struck an iceberg and sank on 15 April 1912.

questions.question: Who became the first person in space in 1961?
questions.explanation: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin orbited Earth in Vostok 1 on 12 April 1961.

questions.question: The Meiji Restoration ended the rule of shoguns from which family?
questions.explanation: The Tokugawa shogunate had ruled since 1603.

questions.question: In which city did the Bolsheviks seize power in October 1917?
questions.explanation: Petrograd was the name of Saint Petersburg at the time.

questions.question: Who was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize?
questions.explanation: Marie Curie shared the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics and later won a second in Chemistry in 1911.

questions.question: Who was Prime Minister of the United Kingdom for most of World War II?
questions.explanation: Churchill led the wartime government from May 1940 to July 1945.

questions.question: The name 'Zimbabwe' is generally traced to a Shona phrase meaning roughly what?
questions.explanation: It comes from dzimba dza mabwe, 'houses of stone'.

questions.question: Which Spanish conquistador led the conquest of the Aztec Empire?
questions.explanation: Cortés landed in 1519 and allied with peoples hostile to the Aztecs.

questions.question: Who was the first emperor of a unified China, founding the Qin dynasty?
questions.explanation: Qin Shi Huang unified China in 221 BC and took the title of first emperor.

questions.question: Which Carthaginian general famously crossed the Alps with elephants to attack Rome?
questions.explanation: Hannibal made the crossing in 218 BC during the Second Punic War.

questions.question: The Rosetta Stone helped scholars decipher which writing system?
questions.explanation: Its text appears in hieroglyphic, Demotic and Greek, which let Champollion crack hieroglyphs in the 1820s.

questions.question: Which Roman emperor ordered the construction of a wall across northern Britain in AD 122?
questions.explanation: Hadrian's Wall marked the northern frontier of Roman Britain.

questions.question: Which war, fought from 431 to 404 BC, pitted Athens against Sparta and their allies?
questions.explanation: Sparta won, ending Athenian dominance.

questions.question: Which of these gaps in time is the LONGEST?
choices: From Cleopatra VII to the fall of Constantinople in 1453
From the fall of Constantinople to the Moon landing
From Cleopatra VII to the Moon landing
From the Great Pyramid of Giza to Cleopatra VII
questions.explanation: The Great Pyramid (about 2560 BC) is about 2,500 years before Cleopatra; the other gaps are about 2,000, 1,480 and 520 years.
questions.misconception: Many people think Cleopatra lived about when the Great Pyramid was built.

questions.question: Whose expedition completed the first circumnavigation of the globe between 1519 and 1522?
questions.explanation: Magellan was killed in the Philippines in 1521. Juan Sebastián Elcano led the surviving ship home.

questions.question: Which empire was ruled by Suleiman the Magnificent?
questions.explanation: Suleiman ruled the Ottoman Empire from 1520 to 1566, at its height of power.

questions.question: In which German city did Gutenberg set up his printing workshop?
questions.explanation: Mainz on the Rhine was his home town and workplace.

questions.question: In which year was Magna Carta sealed by King John of England?
questions.explanation: Magna Carta was sealed at Runnymede in 1215, limiting the king's powers.

questions.question: The Hundred Years' War was fought mainly between which two kingdoms?
questions.explanation: It lasted from 1337 to 1453, with periods of truce, between England and France.

questions.question: Only one reasonably complete Viking-age helmet has been found in Scandinavia. Which find is it?
questions.explanation: The Gjermundbu helmet (10th century) is a rounded cap with a face guard and has no horns. Sutton Hoo is Anglo-Saxon.
questions.misconception: Many people think Viking warriors wore horned helmets in battle.

questions.question: In which year did the Cuban Missile Crisis take place?
questions.explanation: The crisis lasted thirteen days in October 1962 and brought the US and USSR close to nuclear war.

questions.question: Which Belgian king held the Congo Free State as a personal possession?
questions.explanation: The Congo Free State was Leopold's private colony until 1908.

questions.question: In which century BC did Ashoka's reign begin?
questions.explanation: He ruled from about 268 BC.

questions.question: Where was the Olmec heartland?
choices: The Gulf Coast lowlands of Mexico
questions.explanation: It lay in the present-day Mexican states of Veracruz and Tabasco.

questions.question: In which year is the fall of the Western Roman Empire traditionally dated?
questions.explanation: In 476 the last Western emperor, Romulus Augustulus, was deposed by Odoacer.

questions.question: Which Mughal emperor, ruling from 1556 to 1605, is known for his policy of religious tolerance?
questions.explanation: Akbar abolished the tax on non-Muslims and welcomed scholars of many faiths.

questions.question: Which German geographer coined the term 'Silk Road' in 1877?
questions.explanation: The name is modern: Richthofen used Seidenstrasse for these trade routes.
